basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining cardiomyopathy (4/7); skeletal myopathy with muscle mtDNA depletion in 5/5. Seizures 2/7 are below 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal myopathy with muscle mtDNA depletion in 5/5 is common direct muscle disease; cardiomyopathy defines this named subtype.

basis: Neurodevelopmental syndrome; hepatic failure, renal hypoplasia and ASD/hypertension each 1/3. Ocular and limb defects also 1/3, omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: ASD and hypertension each occur in 1/3 (33%); retained with hepatic and renal disease under the cap.
decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment in 1/3 meets the frequency threshold, but is omitted at the cap in favor of hepatic failure, renal hypoplasia and cardiovascular disease.

basis: Intrauterine HSV causes skin injury/scarring (~95%), CNS injury (~65%) and eye damage (~40%); individual CNS malformations at 5-29% do not measure aggregate CNS involvement.

decisions.neurologic: involved: aggregate CNS injury affects ~65% of true intrauterine HSV cases; occasional individual malformations do not exclude common overall CNS damage.
decisions.ocular: involved: destructive congenital ocular lesions, including chorioretinitis and microphthalmia, affect ~40% of intrauterine cases.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: congenital skin lesions and scarring occur in ~95%; this is direct fetal tissue injury, not merely a transient exanthem.

basis: Meningeal tumour; the supplied definition explicitly includes the superior sagittal venous sinus, making neurologic and cardiovascular sites defining.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: superior sagittal venous sinus involvement is explicitly part of the supplied disease definition, rather than inferred from anatomical proximity.

basis: Autoimmune blistering skin manifestation of SLE; renal, blood and joint disease concern underlying systemic lupus, not established direct damage from this cutaneous manifestation.

decisions.haematologic: none: cytopenias concern underlying systemic SLE; direct blood-cell injury attributable to this bullous manifestation is not established in >=30%.
decisions.renal: none: reported nephritis (~50-70%) is separately diagnosed lupus nephritis in underlying SLE; BSLE itself is the blistering skin manifestation.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint disease concerns underlying SLE; common direct joint or muscle injury from this bullous manifestation is not established.

basis: Ceramide storage disorder; destructive Farber arthropathy and SMA-associated muscle wasting commonly (>30%) affect the locomotor system. Other organ frequencies vary across this umbrella.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: destructive arthropathy in Farber disease and muscle wasting in SMA-PME make locomotor impairment common (>30%) across the spectrum.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency with direct T-cell depletion in 3/5 (60%). Pneumonia in 2/5 is a separate infection; thrombocytopenia and intrinsic organ lesions occur in only 1/5.

decisions.haematologic: involved: T-cell lymphopenia is a direct quantitative blood-cell deficit, reported in 3/5 (60%), exceeding the 30% threshold.

basis: Skeletal hyperostosis commonly (>30% each over the course) causes cranial neuropathy, optic damage and hearing loss. Choanal stenosis (1/1) omitted at the cap.

decisions.pulmonary: none: choanal stenosis (1/1) qualifies as airway involvement, but is omitted at the cap in favor of common severe cranial nerve, visual and hearing damage.
decisions.neurologic: involved: progressive cranial nerve compression with facial palsy and intracranial hypertension is characteristic and common (>30%) over the course.

basis: Skin/nail disease and diagnostic oral leukoplakia (4/10); IgA deficiency (4/9) with recurrent infections (3/10) supports immunodeficiency. Anemia occurs in only 1/10.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: documented antibody deficiency (IgA low in 4/9) and recurrent infections (3/10) support immunodeficiency; applicable mechanism axes belong in primary.

basis: Cerebellar neurodevelopmental disease; optic disc pallor in 1/1 assessed supports ocular injury, with very limited sampling. Nystagmus is neurologic; retinal mottling occurs in 1/6.

decisions.ocular: involved: optic disc pallor establishes optic nerve injury in 1/1 assessed; the supplied HPO frequency supports inclusion, with uncertainty from the tiny denominator.
